options.text: moderate, not eating or drinking too much

comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: abstemious eaters, stopping before they feel full
comprehension_question.why_correct: "abstemious" = ölçülü; ipucu: "stopping before they feel full", tek kadeh şarap ve ardından gelen özetleyici kelime "this moderation" (bu ölçülülük).

comprehension_question_2.question_text: What else, besides moderation, explains their long life?

options.text: Strong family ties and daily physical work

comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: together with strong family ties and daily physical work
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: Metin "together with strong family ties and daily physical work" diyor; güçlü aile bağları ve günlük bedensel iş de uzun ömrü açıklar.

paragraph_raw: Burnout is more than ordinary tiredness after a long week. It develops when stress at work continues for months without enough rest or recognition. Sufferers feel enervated, as though all their energy has been drained away, and even small tasks seem impossible. They may also become cynical about their job. Taking a holiday helps only briefly; lasting recovery usually requires changes in workload, clearer boundaries and support from managers.

comprehension_question.question_text: According to the text, what does lasting recovery require?

options.text: Changes in workload, clearer boundaries and support

comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: lasting recovery usually requires changes in workload, clearer boundaries and support from managers
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "lasting recovery usually requires changes in workload, clearer boundaries and support from managers" diyor; tatil kısa süre yardım eder, kalıcı iyileşme iş düzeninin değişmesini ister.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: In the text, the word "enervated" most likely means:
comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: feel enervated, as though all their energy has been drained away
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: "enervated" = takatsiz, bitkin (dikkat: "energetic" ile karıştırılır ama tam tersidir); ipucu: "as though all their energy has been drained away".

paragraph_raw: Almost every cell in the human body follows a circadian rhythm, an internal clock that runs on a cycle of roughly twenty-four hours. This clock tells us when to feel sleepy, when to feel hungry and even when our body temperature should rise. Morning sunlight is the strongest signal that keeps it on time. Night-shift workers, whose clocks are constantly disturbed, have higher rates of heart disease, diabetes and depression.

comprehension_question.question_text: What is the strongest signal that keeps the body clock on time?
comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: Morning sunlight is the strongest signal
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "Morning sunlight is the strongest signal that keeps it on time" diyor; iç saati ayarlayan en güçlü sinyal sabah güneşidir.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: Which group has higher rates of heart disease?
comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: Night-shift workers, whose clocks are constantly disturbed
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: Metin "Night-shift workers, whose clocks are constantly disturbed, have higher rates of heart disease" diyor; gece vardiyası çalışanlarında kalp hastalığı daha sıktır.

paragraph_raw: In the 1840s, the Hungarian doctor Ignaz Semmelweis discovered that many mothers were dying after childbirth because doctors came straight from examining dead bodies without washing their hands. When he ordered his staff to clean their hands with chlorine, deaths fell sharply. Yet his colleagues greeted the idea with derision, laughing at the suggestion that gentlemen's hands could be dirty. He died in poverty, years before his theory was finally accepted.

comprehension_question.question_text: What happened when Semmelweis's staff cleaned their hands with chlorine?
comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: deaths fell sharply
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "When he ordered his staff to clean their hands with chlorine, deaths fell sharply" diyor; klorla el yıkanınca ölümler keskin biçimde düştü.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: In the text, the word "derision" most likely means:
comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: greeted the idea with derision, laughing at the suggestion
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: "derision" = alay, küçümseme; ipucu: "laughing at the suggestion that gentlemen's hands could be dirty" — meslektaşları fikre güldüler.

paragraph_raw: Every day, people die while waiting for a new kidney, liver or heart. The main problem is a dearth of donors: far too few organs are available for the thousands of patients on waiting lists. Some countries have tried to solve this with an opt-out system, in which every adult is treated as a donor unless they have said otherwise. Supporters say it saves lives, while critics argue that donation should always be an active, personal choice.

comprehension_question.question_text: How does an opt-out system work?

options.text: People must pay to become donors
Every adult is a donor unless they say otherwise

comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: every adult is treated as a donor unless they have said otherwise
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "every adult is treated as a donor unless they have said otherwise" diyor; aksini söylemeyen her yetişkin bağışçı sayılır.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: What do critics argue?

options.text: The system does not save lives
Donation should be an active, personal choice

comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: donation should always be an active, personal choice
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: Metin eleştirmenlerin "donation should always be an active, personal choice" dediğini söyler; bağış bilinçli, kişisel bir tercih olmalıdır.

paragraph_raw: Around two billion people still cook over open fires or simple stoves that burn wood, coal or animal dung. In poorly ventilated homes, these fires fill the air with noxious smoke that damages the lungs, especially those of women and young children who spend the most time near the stove. The World Health Organization estimates that this indoor pollution causes millions of early deaths each year. Cleaner stoves are cheap, yet many families still cannot afford them.

comprehension_question.question_text: Who is most affected by the indoor smoke?
comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: especially those of women and young children
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "especially those of women and young children who spend the most time near the stove" diyor; ocağa en yakın olan kadınlar ve küçük çocuklar en çok etkilenir.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: In the text, the word "noxious" most likely means:
comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: noxious smoke that damages the lungs
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: "noxious" = zehirli, zararlı; ipucu hemen ardında: "that damages the lungs" ve sonraki cümlede "millions of early deaths".

paragraph_raw: Malaria still kills more than half a million people each year, most of them children under five in sub-Saharan Africa. The disease is transmitted by mosquitoes that bite mainly at night, which is why bed nets treated with insecticide have become one of the most effective tools against it. Travellers from other regions are usually advised to take prophylactic tablets, beginning before the journey and continuing for several weeks after returning, so that the parasite is destroyed before it can cause illness. Recently, the first malaria vaccines for children have also been approved.

comprehension_question.question_text: Why are bed nets so effective against malaria?

options.text: The nets kill the parasite in the blood
The mosquitoes bite mainly at night

comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: mosquitoes that bite mainly at night, which is why bed nets
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "mosquitoes that bite mainly at night, which is why bed nets..." diyor; sivrisinekler çoğunlukla gece soktuğu için cibinlik çok etkilidir.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: In the text, the word "prophylactic" most likely means:

options.text: taken to cure a disease already present

comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: beginning before the journey and continuing for several weeks after returning, so that the parasite is destroyed before it can cause illness
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: "prophylactic" = önleyici; ipucu: tabletler yolculuktan ÖNCE başlar ve "before it can cause illness" — hastalık başlamadan önlemek için.

paragraph_raw: For much of the twentieth century, people with mental illness faced not only their symptoms but also public opprobrium: they were often described as weak, dangerous or morally flawed, and their families felt ashamed to admit that anyone at home needed help. This harsh judgement kept many sufferers from seeking treatment until their condition became severe. In recent decades, campaigns featuring athletes, actors and ordinary people speaking openly about depression and anxiety have reduced this stigma, although surveys show that negative attitudes remain common, particularly towards serious conditions such as schizophrenia.

comprehension_question.question_text: In the text, the word "opprobrium" most likely means:
comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: public opprobrium: they were often described as weak, dangerous or morally flawed
comprehension_question.why_correct: "opprobrium" = toplumsal kınama; iki noktadan sonra açıklanır: "described as weak, dangerous or morally flawed" ve sonraki cümle "This harsh judgement" der.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: What have recent campaigns done?

options.text: Reduced the stigma around mental illness

comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: have reduced this stigma, although surveys show that negative attitudes remain common
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: Metin kampanyaların "have reduced this stigma" dediğini, ama "negative attitudes remain common" olduğunu söyler; damga azaldı ama bitmedi.

paragraph_raw: In 2016, an American professor lay in a coma, moribund after a drug-resistant bacterial infection had spread through his body, and doctors told his wife that he might die within days. As a last resort, scientists searched sewage and soil for bacteriophages, viruses that attack only specific bacteria while leaving human cells untouched. The carefully selected phages were injected into his bloodstream, and within days he woke up. His recovery revived interest in a treatment that had been largely abandoned in the West after the arrival of antibiotics, although it had continued in parts of Eastern Europe.

comprehension_question.question_text: What are bacteriophages, according to the text?

options.text: Viruses that attack only specific bacteria

comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: viruses that attack only specific bacteria while leaving human cells untouched
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin bakteriyofajları "viruses that attack only specific bacteria while leaving human cells untouched" diye tanımlar; yalnız belirli bakterilere saldıran virüslerdir.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: In the text, the word "moribund" most likely means:
comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: moribund after a drug-resistant bacterial infection had spread through his body, and doctors told his wife that he might die within days
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: "moribund" = ölmek üzere; ipucu: komadaydı ve doktorlar "he might die within days" dedi.

paragraph_raw: A new class of weight-loss drugs, originally developed to treat diabetes, is transforming the treatment of obesity. These medicines copy a natural hormone that the gut releases after a meal, signalling to the brain that the body has eaten enough. Patients who once described themselves as voracious, constantly thinking about food and unable to stop eating, report that their cravings have largely disappeared. In clinical trials, many lost around fifteen percent of their body weight. However, the drugs are expensive, and most patients regain much of the weight once they stop taking them.

comprehension_question.question_text: What happens when most patients stop taking the drugs?

options.text: They regain much of the weight

comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: most patients regain much of the weight once they stop taking them
comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "most patients regain much of the weight once they stop taking them" diyor; ilaç bırakılınca kiloların çoğu geri gelir.

comprehension_question_2.question_text: How do these medicines work?

options.text: They stop the stomach from digesting food
They copy a gut hormone that signals fullness
They make the body burn more energy

comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: copy a natural hormone that the gut releases after a meal, signalling to the brain that the body has eaten enough
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: Metin ilaçların "copy a natural hormone ... signalling to the brain that the body has eaten enough" dediğini söyler; tokluk sinyali veren bağırsak hormonunu taklit ederler.

paragraph_raw: Modern screening technology can detect tiny tumours long before they cause any symptoms. This sounds entirely positive, but it has created a problem known as overdiagnosis. Many small prostate and thyroid cancers are indolent, growing so slowly that they would never have harmed the patient during his or her lifetime. Once discovered, however, they are frequently treated with surgery or radiation, which can cause serious side effects. Doctors are therefore increasingly recommending active surveillance, in which such tumours are monitored regularly and treated only if they start to grow.

comprehension_question.question_text: In the text, the word "indolent" most likely means:

options.text: developing very slowly and causing little harm

comprehension_question.evidence_snippet: indolent, growing so slowly that they would never have harmed the patient
comprehension_question.why_correct: "indolent" = yavaş seyreyen; ipucu virgülden sonra: "growing so slowly that they would never have harmed the patient".

comprehension_question_2.question_text: What is active surveillance?

options.text: Monitoring tumours and treating them only if they grow

comprehension_question_2.evidence_snippet: such tumours are monitored regularly and treated only if they start to grow
comprehension_question_2.why_correct: Metin aktif izlemi "such tumours are monitored regularly and treated only if they start to grow" diye açıklar; tümör düzenli izlenir, büyürse tedavi edilir.

paragraph_raw: During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts later, so teenagers naturally feel sleepy around eleven at night and find it difficult to wake before eight. Schools that begin at half past seven therefore force many students to attend their first lessons in a somnolent state, yawning, struggling to keep their eyes open and absorbing little of what is taught. paragraph_raw: Access to potable water, water that is safe enough to drink without risk of illness, remains one of the greatest divides between rich and poor nations. Around two billion people still depend on sources contaminated with sewage, which spread diseases such as cholera, typhoid and dysentery. Children suffer most: diarrhoea caused by dirty water kills hundreds of thousands under the age of five each year. Simple solutions, including chlorine tablets, ceramic filters and protected wells, can dramatically reduce these deaths, yet they often fail when communities are not involved in maintaining them.

comprehension_question.why_correct: Metin "they often fail when communities are not involved in maintaining them" diyor; topluluk bakıma katılmazsa çözümler başarısız olur.

paragraph_raw: Every summer, some runners collapse during races held on sweltering afternoons, when temperatures climb above thirty-five degrees and the air feels thick and heavy. paragraph_raw: Searching for symptoms online has become a common habit, but it often does more harm than good. paragraph_raw: In 2018, the United Kingdom introduced a levy on soft drinks, charging manufacturers extra for every litre of drink containing more than five grams of sugar per hundred millilitres. paragraph_raw: A stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is suddenly blocked or when a blood vessel in the brain bursts. Doctors teach the public a simple test: ask the person to smile and check whether one side of the face droops, ask them to raise both arms, and listen to their speech. paragraph_raw: Depression is often imagined simply as deep sadness, but one of its most disabling symptoms is anhedonia: sufferers lose the ability to enjoy things that once gave them pleasure, such as music, food, hobbies or time with friends. paragraph_raw: When a pharmaceutical company develops a new medicine, it receives a patent that allows it to be the only seller for around twenty years. During this period, prices can be exorbitant, sometimes reaching thousands of dollars for a single month of treatment, far beyond what most families can pay. paragraph_raw: Human gestation lasts about forty weeks, from the start of the mother's last period until the baby is born. paragraph_raw: Road accidents kill more than a million people every year and are the leading cause of death for young people aged fifteen to twenty-nine. paragraph_raw: For more than a thousand years, European doctors learned anatomy from the books of the Greek physician Galen, who had studied animals rather than humans. paragraph_raw: Childhood obesity has tripled in many countries since the 1970s. Researchers point to two main causes: cheaper, sugar-rich food and an increasingly slothful way of life. paragraph_raw: Organ transplants save thousands of lives every year, but the patient's immune system treats the new kidney or heart as a foreign invader and tries to destroy it. To prevent this, recipients must take immunosuppressant drugs, which deliberately weaken the body's defences, for the rest of their lives. The price of this protection is high: patients become more vulnerable to infections and certain cancers. paragraph_raw: Many parents panic when their child develops a fever and immediately reach for antipyretic medicines such as paracetamol or ibuprofen, which bring the temperature down within an hour. paragraph_raw: Hearing loss affects about two-thirds of people over seventy, yet most wait years before trying a hearing aid, often because they feel embarrassed. Older adults with untreated hearing loss show faster mental attrition, losing memory and thinking skills more quickly than their peers. Scientists believe that the brain, forced to work harder to understand speech, has fewer resources left for other tasks, and that social isolation also plays a role. paragraph_raw: Sloths are arboreal mammals that spend almost their entire lives hanging upside down in the branches of Central and South American rainforests. paragraph_raw: Comets are often described as dirty snowballs: mixtures of ice, dust and rock left over from the formation of the solar system about four and a half billion years ago. Instead, it undergoes sublimation, turning directly from solid into gas because of the extremely low pressure of space. As the Arctic warms nearly four times faster than the global average, the inexorable thaw, which no local effort can stop once it has begun, is releasing this carbon as carbon dioxide and methane, gases that further accelerate warming. paragraph_raw: Tardigrades, microscopic animals less than a millimetre long, are among the toughest creatures on Earth. They live in moss, soil and even on mountain tops, and they can survive conditions that would kill almost any other organism. When their surroundings dry out completely, they survive desiccation by pulling in their legs, losing almost all the water in their bodies and entering a state in which their metabolism nearly stops. In this form, they can remain alive for years, and they return to normal within hours of being placed in water. Some have even survived exposure to outer space.

paragraph_raw: About half of the Earth's surface lies beneath the abyssal plains, vast flat areas of the ocean floor found at depths of three to six kilometres. Sunlight never reaches these depths, the temperature stays just above freezing, and the pressure is hundreds of times greater than at the surface. For a long time, scientists assumed that such conditions could support little life. Deep-sea expeditions have since discovered a surprising variety of creatures, from glass sponges to giant worms, many of which feed on the slow rain of dead material that drifts down from the waters above.

paragraph_raw: Although glass looks and feels like a solid, its internal structure is surprisingly unusual. paragraph_raw: A black hole forms when a massive star collapses under its own gravity, squeezing its matter into an extraordinarily small space. Around it lies a boundary called the event horizon. Anything that crosses this line, whether a planet, a gas cloud or a beam of light, faces an ineluctable fate: no force in the universe can pull it back out, and it will inevitably be drawn towards the centre. For this reason, black holes cannot be seen directly. Astronomers detect them instead by observing how their gravity affects nearby stars and the glowing gas that swirls around them before falling in.

paragraph_raw: For most of the twentieth century, biologists believed that only changes in DNA itself could be passed from parents to children. Research in epigenetics has complicated this picture. Environmental factors such as diet, stress and pollution can attach chemical markers to genes, switching them on or off without altering the underlying code. Some studies suggest that these changes may be heritable: the grandchildren of people who survived a severe famine in the Netherlands in 1944, for example, showed differences in weight and health that seemed to reflect their grandparents' hunger. Scientists, however, still disagree about how common and lasting such effects are in humans.

paragraph_raw: Almost every cell in your body contains hundreds of mitochondria, tiny structures that produce the energy the cell needs. Remarkably, they appear to have begun as independent bacteria. paragraph_raw: Some governments have dreamed of autarky, believing that a nation which produces everything it needs can never be pressured by foreign powers. paragraph_raw: Economists describe money as fungible. A ten-euro note in your pocket is worth exactly the same as any other ten-euro note, and it makes no difference which one you spend. paragraph_raw: Parchment was so expensive in the Middle Ages that monks sometimes scraped old writing off a page and reused it. The result, a palimpsest, often still holds faint traces of the earlier text beneath the new one. The most famous example is a prayer book written in the thirteenth century over a tenth-century copy of works by the Greek mathematician Archimedes. Using special light and X-rays, scientists in the early 2000s recovered much of the hidden text, including a work that was otherwise lost and showed that Archimedes had come surprisingly close to ideas later found in calculus.
